blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Underwater navigation requires translating visual spatial cues into motion, yet marine vision-language datasets rarely include paired robot trajectories. We present NereidVLA, a vision-language-action model that transfers marine spatial knowledge to language-conditioned 3D navigation. We first train Sea2Know on approximately two million marine examples to learn target grounding, spatial relations, and scene structure without paired robot-motion supervision. We then adapt it using expert trajectories executed under simulated underwater vehicle dynamics. Given RGB histories and a language instruction, NereidVLA predicts discrete motion tokens that decode into local 3D trajectories for closed-loop tracking. Evaluation combines an independent six-dimensional underwater navigation understanding benchmark with offline prediction and closed-loop navigation. Under matched navigation training and execution settings, marine spatial pretraining increases simulation success from 72.4% to 84.4%. Without fine-tuning on the real test environment, NereidVLA achieves 78.75% success in laboratory-pool robot trials, compared with 47.50% for InternVLA-N1. These results show that marine spatial supervision can support downstream motion learning and physical underwater navigation.
blocks.zh: 水下导航需要将视觉空间提示转化为运动,然而海洋视觉语言数据集却很少包括配对机器人轨迹. 我们介绍了NereidVLA,一种将海洋空间知识转移到语言条件3D导航的视觉-语言-行动模型。 我们首先训练Sea2 了解大约200万个海洋例子, 学习目标地面,空间关系,和场景结构 没有对机器人-运动监督。 然后我们用在模拟水下飞行器动力学下 执行的专家轨迹来调整它 鉴于RGB历史和一个语言指令,NereidVLA预测解码为本地3D轨迹的离散运动符号,用于闭路跟踪. 评价将独立的六维水下导航理解基准与离线预测和闭路导航相结合。 在相应的导航培训和执行环境下,海洋空间预训将模拟成功率从72.4%提高到84.4%。 如果不对真实的试验环境进行微调,NereidVLA在实验室-池式机器人试验中取得了78.75%的成功,而InternVLA-N1则取得了47.50%的成功. 这些结果显示,海洋空间监督可以支持下游运动学习和物理水下航行.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Language-guided underwater navigation requires robots to interpret a goal
in the context of three-dimensional scene geometry. Following a pipeline
requires understanding its direction and the obstacles nearby, while cave
navigation depends on recognizing entrances and the geometry of traversable
passages. These decisions involve changes in depth as well as horizontal
motion: recognizing the target is only one part of determining how to reach
it. Turbidity, light scattering, changing illumination, and occlusion further
complicate these spatial judgments [ 1 ] .

blocks.en:
Vision-language-action (VLA) models connect visual understanding and language
to robot behavior [ 35 , 13 , 22 ] ,
and recent work has begun to explore this connection in underwater
environments [ 25 , 9 , 29 ] .
Meanwhile, marine vision-language datasets provide rich annotations for
objects, spatial relationships, and scene structure [ 28 , 34 ] . These resources offer an opportunity to learn about the
underwater world, but rarely include paired robot trajectories.
Collecting underwater navigation demonstrations remains costly and difficult
to scale, and spatial understanding alone does not specify how a robot
should move. We therefore investigate a central question: Can spatial knowledge acquired from large-scale marine observations
be transferred to language-conditioned 3D underwater navigation?

blocks.en:
We propose NereidVLA , an underwater VLA model that connects marine
spatial learning with trajectory-supervised navigation adaptation
(Figure 1 ). The first stage establishes spatial knowledge
before learning robot motion. Using available annotations and question-answer
formats from NAUTILUS [ 28 ] and
USI-Brain [ 34 ] , together with underwater simulation data,
we construct approximately two million marine spatial-understanding examples.
We use these examples to train Sea2Know , built on
Qwen3-VL-8B [ 4 ] , to learn target grounding, spatial
relationships, and scene structure. This stage makes marine observations
useful for navigation preparation without requiring paired robot-motion
annotations.

The second stage turns this spatially informed model into a trajectory
predictor for closed-loop navigation. Using 573 simulated scenes in
MarineGym [ 7 ] , we collect 5,117 expert demonstrations
and derive approximately 100,000 navigation examples spanning obstacle
avoidance, target search, pipeline navigation, and cave navigation.
An expert controller executes geometric reference plans under simulated
vehicle dynamics, and the resulting robot motion supplies the trajectory
targets. We use these demonstrations to adapt Sea2Know into NereidVLA,
encoding local body-frame displacements as motion tokens.
Given RGB histories and language instructions, the model autoregressively
predicts local 3D trajectories, which a low-level feedback controller tracks
as visual observations are updated and the trajectory is replanned.

blocks.en:
Our main contributions are as follows: 1. We propose NereidVLA, a two-stage underwater VLA framework that
transfers marine spatial knowledge to language-conditioned local
3D trajectory prediction and closed-loop navigation. 2. We construct a diverse underwater navigation dataset from expert
demonstrations executed under simulated vehicle dynamics, and introduce
an independent six-dimensional underwater navigation understanding
benchmark. 3. We demonstrate improvements in offline trajectory prediction and
closed-loop navigation in simulation and on a real robot.
Matched comparisons establish the benefit of marine spatial pretraining,
while laboratory-pool trials demonstrate transfer to physical execution
without test-environment fine-tuning.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Underwater vision-language understanding. NAUTILUS introduces NautData for underwater captioning, visual
question answering, grounding, and detection, alongside an
imaging-prior-based visual feature enhancement module [ 28 ] .
USI-Brain develops spatial supervision covering object understanding,
spatial relations, depth reasoning, degradation-aware perception,
and scene understanding [ 34 ] .
UWBench evaluates underwater captioning, grounding, and visual
question answering, while MarineEval focuses on marine-domain
knowledge and reasoning [ 31 , 26 ] .
These efforts advance underwater visual understanding and
evaluation but do not provide paired robot-motion supervision.
We use NAUTILUS and USI-Brain data to train Sea2Know
and introduce an independent benchmark for
navigation-relevant spatial judgments.

blocks.en:
The first stage learns navigation-relevant spatial knowledge
from marine visual data without paired robot trajectories.
We construct approximately two million vision-language
training examples using resources from
NAUTILUS [ 28 ] and
USI-Brain [ 34 ] , together with underwater
simulation scene data. We reuse available annotations,
including object categories and bounding boxes, and draw
on existing marine question-answer formats to organize
supervision for target grounding, relative spatial
relations, depth ordering, and scene structure.
For sequential observations, we also construct multi-frame
questions about changes in target position, visibility,
and apparent size. Together, these examples provide
supervision for both static spatial relationships and
temporal changes in underwater scenes.

blocks.en: 3.3 Navigation Demonstration Generation
blocks.zh: 3.3 导航演示生成

blocks.en:
We build a navigation demonstration pipeline on MarineGym [ 7 ] ,
covering five environment families: seabeds, fixed underwater facilities,
pipelines, aquaculture cages, and caves. Each environment varies task goals,
obstacle layouts, and traversable structures, together with water and lighting
conditions.
blocks.zh:
我们在MarineGym上建造一个导航示范管道 [7],
包括五个环境系统:海底、固定水下设施、
管道、水产养殖笼和洞穴。 每一种环境都不同任务目标,
障碍布局、可移动结构以及水和照明
条件。

blocks.en:
Expert references are generated according to the geometry of each task.
For obstacle avoidance and target search, we use 3D path search and collision
checks to obtain feasible routes around obstacles or toward targets. For
pipeline and cave navigation, reference paths additionally follow pipe axes
or cave topology while accounting for local obstructions. Candidate routes
are checked against the robot’s physical envelope and passage constraints.
blocks.zh:
专家参考资料是根据每项任务的几何学生成的。
为了避开障碍和搜索目标,我们使用3D路径搜索和碰撞
检查以获得可行的路线 绕过障碍物或向目标。 对于
管道和洞穴导航,参考路径额外遵循管道轴线
或洞穴地形,同时说明当地的障碍。 候选路线
对照机器人的物理信封和通道限制进行检查。

blocks.en:
We derive trajectory supervision from executed motion , rather than
using the planned paths as training targets. A dynamics-based expert
controller tracks each feasible reference with the simulated underwater robot,
while RGB observations,
robot motion, and task information are recorded in temporal alignment. We
retain valid observation–trajectory segments from demonstrations that satisfy
the relevant task and safety checks.
blocks.zh:
我们从被执行的运动中获得轨迹监督,而不是
将计划的道路作为培训目标。 基于动态的专家
控制器用模拟水下机器人追踪每一个可行的参照物,
当RGB观测时,
机器人运动,和任务信息以时间对齐记录. 我们
保留符合要求的示威中有效的观察-射线段
相关任务和安全检查。

blocks.en:
We execute navigation through receding-horizon prediction
and feedback tracking. After following a short segment
of the predicted five-second trajectory, the robot
updates its visual observations and replans.
To account for inference latency, the predicted trajectory
is transformed into a fixed local execution frame using
the estimated robot pose at image capture time.

Since the VLA predicts positions rather than control
commands, the execution module determines attitude

and declared heading rules, and allocates commands to eight thrusters.
In simulation, replanning occurs at 1 Hz of simulated time.

blocks.en: 4 Experiments
blocks.zh: 4 实验

blocks.en: We evaluate Sea2Know on underwater spatial understanding and NereidVLA on offline 3D trajectory prediction and closed-loop navigation in simulation and on a real robot. We also assess the contribution of marine spatial pretraining.
blocks.zh: 我们评价 " 海2 " 关于水下空间理解的知识,以及 " NereidVLA " 关于离线的3D轨迹预测和闭路导航的模拟和真正的机器人。 我们还评估海洋空间预先训练的贡献。

blocks.en: 4.1 Experimental Setup
blocks.zh: 4.1 实验设置

blocks.en: Using MarineGym [ 7 ] and high-fidelity underwater assets, we construct a training pool of 573 simulated scenes and collect 5,117 expert demonstrations executed under simulated vehicle dynamics. The demonstrations cover obstacle avoidance, target search, pipeline navigation, and cave navigation. We extract 100,000 training samples from 4,597 demonstrations across 516 scenes, with 18,726 samples for validation. Offline prediction uses approximately 10,000 test samples. Both offline testing and closed-loop simulation use 50 independent scenes held out from the navigation training pool, with unseen high-fidelity assets, layouts, and structures.
blocks.zh: 我们利用MarineGym [7] 和高真实度的水下资产,建造了一个由573个模拟场景组成的训练池,并收集了5 117个在模拟车辆动态下执行的专家演示。 示威包括避障、目标搜索、管道导航和洞穴导航。 我们从516场4,597场示威中提取出10万个训练样本,其中18,726个样本进行验证. 离线预测使用约10,000个测试样本. 离线测试和闭路模拟均使用导航训练池外的50个独立场景,这些场景具有看不见的高纯度资产、布局和结构。

blocks.en: Our six-dimensional Underwater Navigation Understanding Benchmark covers target grounding (TGA), spatial relations (SRA), passage structure (TSA), traversability prediction (TPA), temporal understanding (TUA), and local action decisions (LADA). TPA and LADA assess visual judgments of traversable space and plausible local actions, without imposing robot-specific motion constraints. Three trained annotators independently label 4,500 candidate questions and cross-check the annotations, retaining 3,646 after filtering disagreements and low-quality items. The benchmark is strictly disjoint from the Stage 1 training data. Annotation details and additional NautData and UWBench [ 28 , 31 ] results are provided in the supplement.
blocks.zh: 我们的六维水下航行理解基准涵盖目标地面、空间关系、通道结构、可转性预测、时间理解和地方行动决定。 TPA和LADA评估可移动空间的视觉判断和可能的地方行动,而不施加机器人特定的运动限制。 3名经过培训的注释员将4 500个候选问题单独标出,并交叉核对说明,在过滤分歧和低质量物品后保留了3 646个。 基准与第一阶段培训数据严格脱节。 补编提供了注释细节和额外的NautData和UWBench[28,31]结果。

blocks.en: For closed-loop simulation, we evaluate 25 distinct navigation instances for each of the four tasks. Each instance is tested under five lighting and water conditions, giving 500 executions per model. Models tested on the same robot use the same low-level controller and evaluation conditions.
blocks.zh: 就闭路模拟而言,我们评价了四个任务中每个任务的25个不同的导航实例。 每个案例在五个照明和供水条件下进行测试,每个模型有500人被处决。 在同一机器人上测试的模型使用相同的低级控制器和评价条件.

blocks.en: 4.2 Spatial Understanding
blocks.zh: 4.2 空间理解

blocks.en: Table 1 reports results on our six-dimensional underwater navigation understanding benchmark. Sea2Know (8B) outperforms its Qwen3-VL-8B backbone across all six dimensions, with gains of 21.83 points in spatial relations, 28.97 in temporal understanding, and 15.26 in local action decisions . Target grounding improves by a smaller margin of 4.48 points. These gains suggest that marine spatial learning strengthens relational and temporal understanding beyond object recognition and grounding.
blocks.zh: 表1报告我们六维水下导航理解基准的结果。 Sea2Know(8B)在所有六个维度上都超过了其Qune3-VL-8B主干,空间关系收益21.83分,时间理解收益28.97分,地方行动决定收益15.26分. 目标落地率提高4.48分。 这些成果表明,海洋空间学习加强了超出物体识别和搁浅范围的关系和时间理解。

blocks.en: The improvements are consistent across model scales, with Sea2Know (2B, 4B, and 8B) outperforming their respective backbones on all six dimensions. Sea2Know (8B) also surpasses SpatialAxiom-9B across all dimensions, particularly in temporal understanding (67.79% vs. 39.18%) and local action decisions (31.61% vs. 13.90%) . Compared with the navigation-specialized SimpleVLN, Sea2Know (8B) achieves higher scores across all six dimensions on this VQA benchmark, including local action decisions ( 31.61% vs. 7.90% ). Among the evaluated open-weight models, Sea2Know (8B) leads on five dimensions; Qwen3-VL-32B performs slightly better on traversability prediction, while several API-based models achieve higher scores.
blocks.zh: 不同模型尺度的改进是一致的,Sea2Know(2B,4B,8B)在所有六个维度上都超过了各自的骨干. Sea2Know(8B)也超越了空间Axiom-9B的各个层面,特别是在时间理解(67.79%对39.18%)和地方行动决定(31.61%对13.90%)方面。 与导航专业SimpleVLN相比,Sea2Know(8B)在这个VQA基准上在所有六个维度上都取得了更高的分数,包括地方行动决定(31.61%对7.90%). 在被评价的开量模型中,Sea2Know(8B)领先于5维;Qune3-VL-32B在可变性预测上表现略好,而几个基于API的模型则取得了更高的分数.

blocks.en: Figure 3 presents representative examples from the benchmark. On the external NautData and UWBench datasets, Sea2Know also performs well on object grounding, spatial relations, and referring localization, although it trails the strongest baseline on some shape- and size-related tasks. Full results are provided in the supplementary material.
blocks.zh: 图3提供了基准中有代表性的例子。 在外部的NautData和UWBench数据集上,Sea2Know也很好地表现了物体的地面,空间关系,以及转引本地化,虽然它在一些形状和大小相关的任务上追随最强的基线. 补充材料提供了全部结果。

blocks.en: 4.3 Offline Trajectory Prediction
blocks.zh: 4.3 离线轨迹预测

blocks.en: Table 2 presents trajectory prediction results on unseen scenes. NereidVLA achieves the lowest error on four of the five metrics. Compared with SimpleVLN, the closest competitor, it reduces ADE by 2.3% , FDE by 6.1% , and Z MAE by 14.1% .
blocks.zh: 表2列出了未见场景的轨迹预测结果。 NereidVLA在5个度量衡中实现4个最小误差. 与最接近的竞争对手SimpleVLN相比,它将ADE减少2.3%,FDE减少6.1%,Z MAE减少14.1%。

blocks.en:
Lower Z MAE indicates more accurate vertical motion
prediction, important for 3D underwater navigation.
blocks.zh:
下 Z MAE 表示更精确的垂直运动
预测,对于3D水下导航很重要.

blocks.en: NereidVLA achieves the lowest FDE P95 but a slightly higher ADE P95 than SimpleVLN, indicating lower high-percentile endpoint errors but not uniformly lower trajectory errors.

blocks.en: 4.4 Closed-loop Navigation
blocks.zh: 4.4 闭路导航

blocks.en:
We evaluate closed-loop navigation with repeated
observations, replanning, and feedback tracking.
Success requires task completion within the time
limit without safety violations; task-specific
criteria appear in the supplement.
blocks.zh:
我们评价闭路导航
观察、重新规划和反馈跟踪。
成功需要及时完成任务
限制,不违反安全规定;
标准见补编。

blocks.en:
As shown in Table 3 ,
NereidVLA achieves an overall success rate of 84.4% , exceeding Qwen3-VL-8B (72.4%)
by 12.0 percentage points . It also achieves
the highest Grid-SPL (81.85%) and lowest Jerk RMS
(1.0658), indicating favorable path efficiency and
motion smoothness.
blocks.zh:
如表3所示,
NereidVLA的总成功率达到84.4%,超过了Qune3-VL-8B(72.4%)
12.0个百分点 也实现了

(1.0658),显示有利于路径效率和
运动光滑。

blocks.en:
Relative to Qwen3-VL-8B, the largest gains occur in target search
(52.0% to 81.6% ) and pipeline navigation
(71.2% to 86.4% ), with smaller gains in obstacle
avoidance and cave navigation. InternVLA-N1 [ 12 ] slightly exceeds NereidVLA on pipeline navigation
(87.2% versus 86.4%). Figure 4 (a)
shows representative predicted and executed trajectories.

相对于Qune3-VL-8B,最大的收益出现在目标搜索中
(52.0%至81.6%)和管道导航
(71.2%至86.4%),障碍收益较小
躲避和洞穴航行。 InternVLA-N1[12]略超过 NereidVLA 关于管道导航

blocks.en: We deploy NereidVLA on a BlueROVHeavy robot in a laboratory pool without fine-tuning on data from the real test environment. RGB observations are sent to a remote RTX 4090 server for asynchronous planning and local 3D trajectory prediction. The predicted trajectories are then tracked by a low-level controller using IMU-based state feedback.
blocks.zh: 我们把NereidVLA 部署在BlueROVHEAVY机器人上 在一个实验室池里,没有精细地调整来自真实测试环境的数据。 RGB观测结果被发送到远程RTX 4090服务器,用于同步规划和本地3D轨迹预测. 然后由低级控制器利用IMU的状态反馈来跟踪预测的轨迹.

blocks.en: We evaluate each model on four tasks: target approach, obstacle avoidance, goal approach with obstacles, and narrow-passage avoidance, conducting 20 trials per task with varied target positions and obstacle layouts. A trial is successful if the robot completes the task without collision. The two target-approach tasks require reaching within 1.5 m of the target, while narrow-passage navigation requires crossing the designated endpoint.
blocks.zh: 我们评价每个模式的四项任务:目标办法、避免障碍办法、目标办法有障碍办法和狭窄通道办法,每项任务进行20次试验,确定不同目标位置和障碍布局。 如果机器人在不发生碰撞的情况下完成任务,试验就成功. 两项目标进取任务需要在目标1.5米以内达到,而窄通道导航则需要穿越指定的终点.

blocks.en: As shown in Table 4 , NereidVLA succeeds in 63 of 80 trials (78.75%) , outperforming InternVLA-N1 (47.50%) and Qwen3-VL-8B (35.00%) by 31.25 and 43.75 percentage points , respectively.

blocks.en: 4.5 Ablation and Analysis
blocks.zh: 4.5 分析和分析

blocks.en:
To isolate spatial pretraining, we compare
Sea2Know-initialized NereidVLA with Qwen3-VL-8B
fine-tuned directly on the same 3D trajectory
demonstrations, using matched representations,
supervision, and execution settings.
As shown in Table 2 ,
Sea2Know initialization reduces ADE from 0.29121 to
0.18082 (37.9%) and FDE from 0.55396 to 0.34970
(36.9%). The gains extend to closed-loop navigation,
where simulation success increases from 72.4% to 84.4%
and real-robot success from 35.0% to 78.75%.
These results show that marine spatial pretraining
improves 3D trajectory learning beyond what is achieved
through direct navigation fine-tuning alone.

The benefits of spatial pretraining vary across tasks. In simulation, success improves by 29.6 percentage points in target search and 15.2 points in pipeline navigation, compared with 1.6 points in both obstacle avoidance and cave navigation. Target search requires updating the relative
direction of a language-specified goal as views
change, while pipeline navigation relies on
structural direction and nearby free space.
These demands align with Sea2Know’s gains in
spatial relations and temporal understanding.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We presented NereidVLA, a two-stage framework connecting marine
spatial understanding with language-conditioned 3D underwater
navigation. Sea2Know learns navigation-relevant spatial knowledge
from large-scale marine observations; we then adapt it for 3D
motion prediction using dynamics-grounded demonstrations.
Encoding 3D trajectories as discrete motion tokens enables
autoregressive prediction from visual histories and language
instructions, with feedback tracking for closed-loop execution.
Evaluations spanning spatial understanding, offline prediction,
simulation, and real-robot navigation validate this approach.
With matched downstream settings, Sea2Know initialization improves
simulation success from 72.4% to 84.4%, while NereidVLA
achieves 78.75% real-robot success without test-environment
fine-tuning. These results demonstrate that marine spatial
knowledge can be effectively transferred to language-conditioned
3D trajectory prediction and closed-loop underwater navigation.

blocks.en: Appendix B Data Construction and Understanding Benchmark
blocks.zh: 附录B 数据构建和理解基准

blocks.en: B.1 Marine spatial training data
blocks.zh: B.1 海洋空间培训数据

blocks.en:
Sea2Know is trained on approximately two million marine vision–language
examples from NAUTILUS [ 28 ] , USI-Brain [ 34 ] ,
and underwater simulation scenes. Existing annotations and question–answer
formats provide supervision for target grounding, spatial relations, depth
ordering, and scene structure. Multi-frame questions additionally describe
changes in target position, visibility, and apparent size. None of these
examples requires paired robot trajectories.

Sea2Know接受了大约200万种海洋视觉语言的培训
例如NAUTILUS [28],USI-Brain [34],
和水下模拟场景 现有说明和问答
格式提供目标地面、空间关系、深度的监督
命令和场景结构 多框架问题
目标位置、可见度和明显大小的变化。 没有一个
实例需要配对的机器人轨道。

blocks.en:

Stage 1 training. The external NautData test split is also excluded.

水下航行理解基准与

blocks.en: B.2 Understanding benchmark
blocks.zh: B.2 理解基准

blocks.en:
Our benchmark evaluates six navigation-related judgments
(Figure 3 ): target grounding (TGA),
spatial relations (SRA), passage structure (TSA), traversability
prediction (TPA), temporal understanding (TUA), and local action
decisions (LADA). TUA uses four-frame observations. TPA and LADA assess
visually plausible passage and action choices, rather than vehicle
motion under dynamics constraints.
blocks.zh:
我们的基准评估了6项与导航有关的判决
(图3):目标地面(TGA),
空间关系、通道结构、可转性
预测(TPA)、时间理解(TUA)和地方行动
决定(LADA)。 TUA使用四帧观测. TPA和土地退化评估
视似可行的通道和行动选择,而不是工具
动在动态限制下。

blocks.en:
Three trained annotators independently labeled 4,500 candidate
questions and cross-checked the annotations. After removing disputed and low-quality items,
3,646 remain. Accuracy follows the answer format of each question. For
multi-answer LADA questions, a prediction is correct only if its
selected options exactly match the reference set.
blocks.zh:
3名受过训练的注释员将4 500名候选人单独贴上标签
提问和交叉核对说明。 在移除有争议的低质量物品后,
还有3 646人。 准确性遵循每个问题的答案格式。 对于
多答题 旱地退化评估问题,只有当预测
选择的选项与参考集完全匹配。

blocks.en: B.3 Navigation demonstrations
blocks.zh: B.3 导航演示

blocks.en:
We construct navigation scenes in MarineGym [ 7 ] across five environments: seabeds, fixed underwater facilities, pipelines,
aquaculture cages, and caves. The training pool contains 573 scenes and
5,117 expert demonstrations. From 4,597 demonstrations in 516 scenes,
we extract 100,000 training samples, with 18,726 additional validation
samples. Offline evaluation uses approximately 10,000 test samples;
both offline and closed-loop tests use 50 independent held-out scenes
with unseen assets, layouts, and structures.

while RGB images, instructions, and vehicle motion are recorded in
temporal alignment. We retain valid segments and use the executed trajectories, not the planned paths, as training targets.

blocks.en: Appendix C Training and Baseline Adaptation
blocks.zh: 附录C 培训和基线适应

blocks.en: C.1 Stage 1: Sea2Know training
blocks.zh: C.1 第一阶段:海上知识培训

blocks.en:
We train Sea2Know at 2B, 4B, and 8B scales through full-parameter
supervised fine-tuning of size-matched Qwen3-VL-Instruct backbones.
The vision encoder, vision–language merger, and language model are all
updated. Sea2Know (8B) initializes the navigation model.

我们在2B、4B和8B的天平上训练海2
监督调整大小匹配的Qwen3-VL-指令骨干.
视觉编码器、视觉-语言合并和语言模型

blocks.en: C.2 Stage 2: navigation adaptation
blocks.zh: C.2 阶段2:导航适应

blocks.en:
Given four RGB observations and a language instruction, NereidVLA
predicts ten motion tokens followed by EOS, representing a five-second
local 3D trajectory. We freeze the vision encoder and fully update the
language model, token embeddings, and LM head, without LoRA. The loss is
cross-entropy over the motion tokens and EOS; visual and text context
tokens are masked. We use neither coordinate-regression nor reasoning-text
supervision.

考虑到四个RGB观察和一个语言指令,NereidVLA
预测EOS之后的10个运动符号,代表5秒
本地三维轨道。 我们冻结视觉编码器 并全面更新
语言模型,符号嵌入,和LM头,没有LORA. 损失是
横跨运动符号和 EOS; 视觉和文本上下文
标志是蒙面的。 我们既不使用坐标折返,也不使用推理文字
监督。

blocks.en:
Training uses 100,000 samples for one epoch (391 optimizer steps) on
32 NVIDIA A800 80GB GPUs across four nodes. A microbatch of one per GPU
and eight gradient-accumulation steps give a global batch size of 256.
We use AdamW ( β 1 = 0.9 \beta_{1}=0.9 , β 2 = 0.999 \beta_{2}=0.999 ; weight decay 0.01 0.01 ) with
a learning rate of 10 − 5 10^{-5} , linearly warmed up over 80 steps and then
held constant. Training uses BF16 and fully sharded data parallelism
(FSDP). A fixed subset of 1,024 validation samples is used for monitoring.

blocks.en: C.3 Motion tokenization
blocks.zh: C.3 动议代号

blocks.en:
The ten future positions are expressed in the forward–left–up body
frame fixed at decision time. We cluster displacements from the navigation
training set into a fixed codebook of 1,024 entries. At each step, the
token is chosen from the residual between the target position and the
previously reconstructed waypoint, allowing subsequent tokens to correct
quantization errors. At inference, cumulative codebook displacements
recover the local 3D trajectory. The encoding equations are given in the
main Method section.

blocks.en: E.1 Hardware and execution
blocks.zh: E.1 硬件和执行

blocks.en:
We deploy a BlueROVHeavy with eight thrusters in a laboratory pool.
RGB observations from a RealSense D435i are processed asynchronously
on a remote RTX 4090 server. The predicted waypoints are tracked by a
low-level controller using IMU-supported state estimation, PID feedback,
and dynamics feedforward.

使用IMU支持的状态估计,PID反馈的低级控制器,
和动力向前进。

blocks.en:
To account for inference latency, each trajectory is transformed into
a fixed execution frame using the estimated robot pose at image-capture
time. The robot follows a short segment before acquiring new observations
and replanning. No data from the real test environment are used for
fine-tuning.

blocks.en: E.2 Tasks and success criteria

blocks.en:
We test four tasks with 20 trials per task and model, varying target
positions and obstacle layouts. Success requires completing the task
without collision. Target approach (TA) and goal approach with
obstacles (GA) require reaching within 1.5 m of the target.
Narrow-passage avoidance (NP) requires crossing the specified endpoint;
obstacle avoidance (OA) requires reaching its assigned objective.
All models share the low-level controller and evaluation conditions.
